newsitem.title: USA: Hearing promised on Milwaukee Brewer stadium bill.
newsitem.headline: Hearing promised on Milwaukee Brewer stadium bill.

text.p: The head of a Wisconsin Senate committee has pledged to hold a hearing on a controversial bill affecting a $250 million stadium for the Milwaukee Brewers baseball team and to report the measure out of committee in May.

State Sen. Lynn Adelman, D-New Berlin, made the comments Tuesday when questions about the legality of the bill resulted in an 18 to 15 vote to send the measure to his judiciary committee, according to Phil Calabrese, the committee's clerk.

Calabrese said Wednesday the committee has already contacted the Wisconsin Attorney General's Office for a legal opinion on the bill, as well as lawyers for the Southeast Wisconsin Professional Baseball Park District, a state-created agency overseeing the stadium project.
District officials have said the measure, which would cap the use of local sales tax revenues for the ballpark, was unconstitutional and would likely kill the stadium project if passed.
Calabrese said the judiciary committee would look into questions of whether the bill would alter the powers of the district -- a move specifically prohibited by a law that created the district.
He added that the district's bond counsel would be consulted to determine if the bill would impair the district's contract with bondholders.
The district on March 5 sold $146.7 million of tax-exempt, sales tax revenue bonds backed by a 0.1 percent, five-county sales tax and insured by MBIA Insurance Corp.
Calabrese said the committee could hold a hearing on the bill early next month.
The bill, which passed the Senate Economic Development, Housing and Government Operations Committee on Monday, had been pending before the full Senate Tuesday for a vote.

State Sen. Joe Wineke, D-Verona introduced the bill earlier this month. The measure would set a $160 million bond limit for the district and prohibit any of the sales tax revenues from being used to make lease payments for stadium costs.
The remaining $90 million of the stadium's financing would come from the sale of naming rights, loans to the Brewers and other sources.
